question: How do prompting, supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning differ when used for query rewriting, and what advantages does each approach offer?
answer:
Prompting approaches use specific prompts to guide the LLM's output, providing flexibility and interpretability [page 9, section "3.3 Approaches"]. For zero-shot rewriting, the model uses its pre-existing knowledge to generate expanded terms without prior domain examples [page 10, section "3.3.1 Prompting."].

Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) techniques adapt pre-trained LLMs specifically for query rewriting [page 9, section "3.3 Approaches"]. This method requires an appropriate training dataset [page 10, section "3.3.2 SFT."], and in the context of e-commerce search, dataset creation can be simplified by using data from a system's previous-generation rewriting policies [page 10, section "3.3.2 SFT."].

Reinforcement learning (RL) improves performance by utilizing feedback signals from ranking models or downstream LLM readers [page 11, section "3.3.3 RL."]. RL addresses the issue of scarce training data by incorporating feedback from downstream applications [page 10, section "3.3 Approaches."], which aligns the objective of the query rewriter more closely with the goals of downstream tasks and enhances overall system performance [page 11, section "3.3.3 RL."].

sources.quote: The utilization of LLMs in query rewriting can be categorized into three primary methodologies: prompting, supervised fine-tuning (SFT), and reinforcement learning (RL).
“SFT” and “RL” denote supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning, respectively.
Though prompting method is effective, LLMs are not naturally designed for query rewriting task.

Recently, research [311] has also shown that the LLMs that are pre-trained without any supervised instruction fine-tuning (such as LLaMA) also yield robust zero-shot ranking ability.

By fine-tuning LLMs on task-specific ranking datasets, such as the MS MARCO passage ranking dataset [178], which includes signals of both relevance and irrelevance, LLMs can adjust their parameters to yield better performance in the reranking tasks.
